long_rule.text: An hour counts only if it is in a spell of at least 2 hours without a break. We find the spells for each day separately.

targets.name: Connecting Ridge

'Shackleton - de Gerlache Connecting Ridge' is how the LRO camera team titles a terrain model of the ridge, so the longer name is in use and says where the ridge is, but it is not the name on a NASA list of candidate regions.
targets.list_line: It is on the NASA list of 13 candidate regions of 2022. It is not one of the nine regions that NASA kept in 2024.
targets.list_summary: On the 2022 list of 13 as 'Connecting Ridge'. Not among the nine regions kept in October 2024. The NASA abstract says the cut 'does not imply that removed regions are unsuitable for future exploration'.
targets.why: It is one of the 13 NASA candidate regions for Artemis III of 2022 ('Connecting Ridge'). It is not one of the nine regions kept in 2024. NASA Goddard studied the light on the 5 m models. This region has the most area that is in sunlight for more than 70 % of the time.

'Mons Mouton Plateau' is a different, larger region to the north, and the page shows it separately. No NASA text says 'renamed'.

snow.measured_cells_use: the snow-free odds as the snow maps give them

cloud.source: NASA POWER, POWER Climatology API v2.10.1, regional endpoint; data source named by the service: SYN1DEG (CERES SYN1deg)
cloud.units: percent of sky covered, monthly mean, January first
cloud.what_it_is: Monthly mean share of the sky covered by cloud, in percent, averaged over all hours of the day and night and over the years of the period, for the 1 degree grid box that holds the cell centre (CERES SYN1deg cloud amount as served by NASA POWER). Many cells share one box.
cloud.what_it_is_not: Not the chance that a low Sun is visible. A Sun a few degrees above the horizon shines through a long slanted path, so the same share of cloud hides it more often than it hides a high Sun. The figure is a mean over the whole day and over a box about 111 km tall, not over the hours of low Sun at the cell, and it says nothing about fog or local weather. It enters no score.

cloud_pct_day.meaning: the same mean over daylight hours only; null in months without daylight
cloud_pct_day.source: NASA POWER, POWER Climatology API v2.10.1, regional endpoint; data source named by the service: SYN1DEG, POWER (CERES SYN1deg)

cloud_pct_night.meaning: the same mean over night hours only; null in months without night
cloud_pct_night.source: NASA POWER, POWER Climatology API v2.10.1, regional endpoint; data source named by the service: SYN1DEG, POWER (CERES SYN1deg)

cloud.null_rule: cloud_pct is null when no month has a value; a single month without a value is null inside the list
cloud.cell_to_grid: the 1 degree box that holds the cell centre (lat, lon of grazing_cells.json); grid = [lat, lon] of the box centre
cloud.resolution_note: the service answers on a 1 degree grid, but polewards of 45 degrees neighbouring boxes along a latitude carry the same or nearly the same value in groups (CERES nested grid: about 2 degrees of longitude from 45 to 70, 4 from 70 to 80, 8 from 80 to 89)
cloud.request_rules_followed: one parameter and at most 10 x 10 degrees per request, one request at a time, no key, no login

scale.how: One scale for all the lunar regions, every step and both poles: the top is the first round figure above the 99th percentile of the hours on snow-free ground (north, measured snow) and in the rock season (south). year_h is for a whole year or half-year, period_h for one ten-day period.

horizon_bins.note: The horizons of horizon_cells.json give the open share at the old nine bins only. Each new bin takes the share of the old bin that holds its lower edge. For the four regions of the first build, this gives the same hours after hills as that build. Some regions have a band in which each bin starts at an old edge. For these regions, the hours after hills use the full method of the first build. For the other regions, the hours after hills are a lower bound: with the open share at each new edge, more hours can count. The full method is also an approximation. It counts the Sun as seen from a point only if the whole bin of Sun height is above the horizon of the point. It uses 36 directions of 10 degrees.
horizon_bins.page_text: For 14 of the 16 lunar regions, the hours after hills are a lower bound. The project has the horizons of the areas at nine bins of Sun height only. A new run of the horizon step at each Sun ceiling can increase these hours. For Connecting Ridge and Connecting Ridge Extension, these hours use the full method of the first build.

search_edge.text: For Mons Mouton Plateau, Amundsen Rim, Nobile Rim 2 and Peak near Cabeus B, a strip of Earth south of 59 degrees north also has spells of 2 hours, but the search does not include it.
